None of these are represented anywhere in the proposed IR's four Applicable Rate nodes, which compute the rate purely as a function of the current TNLR value. A hypothetical transaction where a Borrower is delinquent in delivering quarterly financials would, under the source text, be charged the Category 1 (highest) rate regardless of its actual computed TNLR, but the proposed IR would compute whatever rate the actual TNLR produces — potentially a materially lower rate. This is a real, independently operative discrepancy that changes the compliance/pricing conclusion.'

The retrieved context bundle even shows this definition already decomposed into CHILD_RULE nodes for clauses (a) and (b), indicating the definition was recognized as structurally significant, yet the proposed IR contains no 'Acquisition' entry whatsoever, nor entries for the great majority of other defined terms in this section. The deterministic signals corroborate this: 8 enumerated sub-clauses with 0 compiled rules, 16 proviso/exception markers with 0 recorded conditions, and 4 distinct entity-scope terms (Loan Party, Restricted Subsidiary, Borrower, etc.) with no entity-scope restriction recorded anywhere in the IR. Because the artifact does not disclose (at an aggregate level) that its definitional coverage of Section 1.01 is only a small, seemingly arbitrary subset, this omission is not offset by an honest disclosure comparable to the individual PARTIAL/UNSUPPORTED markings on the five terms that were included.

By contrast, the individual PARTIAL/UNSUPPORTED markings on Alternate Base Rate, Adjusted Daily Simple SOFR, Adjusted Term SOFR Rate, Applicable Rate, and Available Amount each candidly disclose why the compiler could not represent the relevant calculation (MAX/SUBTRACT type-check failures, multi-column grid limitations) and are not themselves treated as findings, consistent with the principle that an honest disclosure of a real limitation is not a semantic defect. The problem flagged here is the silent, undisclosed absence of the remaining bulk of the section's definitions, several of which are simple and clearly compilable, and at least one of which (Acquisition) carries independently operative entity-scope content that the deterministic AMBIGUOUS signals specifically call out as missing.'

candidates.normalizedSemantics: OTHER_MATERIAL_SEMANTIC_DISCREPANCY: The source defines Acquired EBITDA not as a simple alias for the defined term 'EBITDA', but as a distinct metric computed by taking the EBITDA methodology and substituting every reference to 'the Company and its Restricted Subsidiaries' with 'such Acquired Entity or Business and its subsidiaries.' In other words, Acquired EBITDA is the acquired target's own stand-alone EBITDA calculated under the same formula, not the Company's consolidated EBITDA. The proposed IR instead models the calculationExpression as a bare DEFINED_TERM_REFERENCE to 'EBITDA' with no substitution/scoping mechanism at all - meaning as compiled, Acquired EBITDA would literally resolve to the Company's own consolidated EBITDA rather than the acquired business's EBITDA. This is a materially different economic result: e.g., if the Company's consolidated EBITDA is $50,000,000 and a small acquired business has its own EBITDA of $5,000,000, the correct Acquired EBITDA add-back (used elsewhere, e.g., in the EBITDA definition's clause (a)(xviii)(a) pro forma add-back for recently acquired entities) should be $5,000,000, but the proposed IR's formula would instead resolve to $50,000,000, a nine-fold overstatement. Although the definition is marked sufficiency PARTIAL rather than COMPLETE, the calculationExpression itself is not marked UNSUPPORTED - it makes an affirmative (and wrong) formula assertion, which is exactly the kind of confident-but-wrong representation this review is meant to catch, distinguishing it from an honest disclosure of a gap.

cases.groundTruthSemanticDescription: Flush valuation rules for Sections 5.15 and 6.04: designating a Subsidiary as Unrestricted is an 'investment' equal to the Company's proportionate share of the fair market value of that Subsidiary's net assets at designation; upon redesignation as Restricted, a permanent deemed investment remains equal to the original investment less the proportionate net asset fair market value at redesignation (if positive); and property transferred to or from an Unrestricted Subsidiary is valued at fair market value at transfer.

OTHER_MATERIAL_SEMANTIC_DISCREPANCY: Section 1.01 defines a very large number of terms, many trivially representable (e.g., 'Account Debtor' means any Person obligated on an Account; 'Agreed Currency' means dollars or any Alternative Currency), and at least one - 'Acquisition' - carries real operative/entity-scope content (restricting qualifying transactions to 'any Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary', with two alternative tests in clauses (a) and (b)). The retrieved context bundle even shows this definition already decomposed into CHILD_RULE nodes for clauses (a) and (b), indicating the definition was recognized as structurally significant, yet the proposed IR contains no 'Acquisition' entry whatsoever, nor entries for the great majority of other defined terms in this section. The deterministic signals corroborate this: 8 enumerated sub-clauses with 0 compiled rules, 16 proviso/exception markers with 0 recorded conditions, and 4 distinct entity-scope terms (Loan Party, Restricted Subsidiary, Borrower, etc.) with no entity-scope restriction recorded anywhere in the IR. A downstream reviewer relying on this IR for the meaning of 'Acquisition' - which gates whether a transaction by, say, an Unrestricted Subsidiary or a non-Loan-Party affiliate qualifies as a Permitted Acquisition elsewhere in the agreement - would find no representation of that entity-scope limitation at all, and could reach a different conclusion about what counts as an 'Acquisition' than the real source text supports. Because the artifact does not disclose (at an aggregate level) that its definitional coverage of Section 1.01 is only a small, seemingly arbitrary subset, this omission is not offset by an honest disclosure comparable to the individual PARTIAL/UNSUPPORTED markings on the five terms that were included.

By contrast, the individual PARTIAL/UNSUPPORTED markings on Alternate Base Rate, Adjusted Daily Simple SOFR, Adjusted Term SOFR Rate, Applicable Rate, and Available Amount each candidly disclose why the compiler could not represent the relevant calculation (MAX/SUBTRACT type-check failures, multi-column grid limitations) and are not themselves treated as findings, consistent with the principle that an honest disclosure of a real limitation is not a semantic defect. The problem flagged here is the silent, undisclosed absence of the remaining bulk of the section's definitions, several of which are simple and clearly compilable, and at least one of which (Acquisition) carries independently operative entity-scope content that the deterministic AMBIGUOUS signals specifically call out as missing.'

candidates.normalizedSemantics: WRONG_POSTURE: The second sentence of §1.07 is a self-executing, present-tense contractual designation ('are hereby designated') that operates automatically upon execution/whenever Subordinated Indebtedness exists, independent of any act by a Loan Party. The opening phrase 'Without limiting the foregoing' expressly signals that this designation is additional to, and not contingent on performance of, the Borrower's separate covenant in the first sentence to 'take or cause ... to take all such actions as shall be necessary.' The proposed IR nonetheless represents this second rule with posture 'OBLIGATION' and entityScope ['LOAN_PARTY'], i.e., as an action-based duty imposed on the Loan Party. This mischaracterizes the legal effect: there is no Loan Party act or omission that could put this designation into or out of effect - it is automatically true by virtue of the Agreement's own language. A downstream compliance/monitoring consumer of the IR could wrongly treat this as an unperformed obligation capable of breach (e.g., requiring evidence the Loan Party 'did' something), when in fact the senior/designated-senior status attaches automatically and is not conditioned on Loan Party performance. This is a real difference in legal posture (self-operative declaration vs. an obligation owed by an entity) that could change a reviewer's compliance or enforcement analysis.

excerpts: ...as "senior indebtedness" and as "designated senior indebtedness" and words of similar import under and in respect of any indenture or other agreement or instrument under which such Subordinated Indebtedness is outstanding and are further given all such other designations as shall be required under the terms of any such Subordinated Indebtedness in order that the Lenders may have and exercise any payment blockage or other remedies available or potentially available to holders of senior indebtedness under the terms of such Subordinated Indebtedness.
candidates.normalizedSemantics: OTHER_MATERIAL_SEMANTIC_DISCREPANCY: The second operative sentence of §1.07 has two distinct operative components: (1) an enumerated designation of the Secured Obligations as 'senior indebtedness' and 'designated senior indebtedness' (and similar words), and (2) a separate, broader catch-all clause under which the Secured Obligations 'are further given all such other designations as shall be required under the terms of any such Subordinated Indebtedness' in order for Lenders to exercise payment-blockage or other senior-creditor remedies. This catch-all is independently operative: it extends the self-executing designation to labels or defined terms used in a particular subordinated debt instrument that may not be 'senior indebtedness' or 'designated senior indebtedness' verbatim (e.g., a custom defined term in a specific indenture). The proposed IR's second rule quotes only the enumerated-label portion of the sentence and its description/condition do not reference the sweep-up catch-all at all, so a reader relying on the IR could wrongly conclude that the designation is limited to the two enumerated labels, potentially missing that Lenders/Agent are entitled to whatever additional designation a specific Subordinated Indebtedness instrument requires. The rule is marked sufficiency PARTIAL, which is an honest general disclosure, but it does not specifically flag that this particular catch-all clause is the gap, so the omission is still worth surfacing on its own terms. I mark this UNCERTAIN rather than MATERIAL because this is largely boilerplate intended to preserve enforceability of payment-blockage rights vis-à-vis third-party subordinated noteholders, and is unlikely by itself to change a capacity, basket, or covenant-compliance conclusion under the Credit Agreement itself, but could matter in an actual subordination/enforcement dispute.

OTHER_MATERIAL_SEMANTIC_DISCREPANCY: Section 1.01 defines a very large number of terms, many trivially representable (e.g., 'Account Debtor' means any Person obligated on an Account; 'Agreed Currency' means dollars or any Alternative Currency), and at least one - 'Acquisition' - carries real operative/entity-scope content (restricting qualifying transactions to 'any Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary', with two alternative tests in clauses (a) and (b)). The retrieved context bundle even shows this definition already decomposed into CHILD_RULE nodes for clauses (a) and (b), indicating the definition was recognized as structurally significant, yet the proposed IR contains no 'Acquisition' entry whatsoever, nor entries for the great majority of other defined terms in this section. The deterministic signals corroborate this: 8 enumerated sub-clauses with 0 compiled rules, 16 proviso/exception markers with 0 recorded conditions, and 4 distinct entity-scope terms (Loan Party, Restricted Subsidiary, Borrower, etc.) with no entity-scope restriction recorded anywhere in the IR. A downstream reviewer relying on this IR for the meaning of 'Acquisition' - which gates whether a transaction by, say, an Unrestricted Subsidiary or a non-Loan-Party affiliate qualifies as a Permitted Acquisition elsewhere in the agreement - would find no representation of that entity-scope limitation at all, and could reach a different conclusion about what counts as an 'Acquisition' than the real source text supports. Because the artifact does not disclose (at an aggregate level) that its definitional coverage of Section 1.01 is only a small, seemingly arbitrary subset, this omission is not offset by an honest disclosure comparable to the individual PARTIAL/UNSUPPORTED markings on the five terms that were included.

By contrast, the individual PARTIAL/UNSUPPORTED markings on Alternate Base Rate, Adjusted Daily Simple SOFR, Adjusted Term SOFR Rate, Applicable Rate, and Available Amount each candidly disclose why the compiler could not represent the relevant calculation (MAX/SUBTRACT type-check failures, multi-column grid limitations) and are not themselves treated as findings, consistent with the principle that an honest disclosure of a real limitation is not a semantic defect. The problem flagged here is the silent, undisclosed absence of the remaining bulk of the section's definitions, several of which are simple and clearly compilable, and at least one of which (Acquisition) carries independently operative entity-scope content that the deterministic AMBIGUOUS signals specifically call out as missing.'

cases.groundTruthSemanticDescription: Liens securing the Secured Obligations are permitted without a dollar cap - an unconditional, non-quantitative permission scoped to a defined obligation pool rather than a basket amount. thresholdValue/thresholdUnit are optional on CandidateContractRuleSchema, so an uncapped permission scoped by definedTermRefs rather than a number is not blocked. Noted only because ContractRuleType's name ('QUANTITATIVE_PERMISSION') reads as if every instance must carry a number - it does not, but a naive extractor could wrongly infer a missing/zero threshold means 'not representable' rather than 'uncapped by definition'. Nomenclature risk, not a schema gap.

cases.groundTruthSemanticDescription: Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA: Consolidated Net Income plus a long, itemized stack of addbacks (interest expense, taxes, D&A, non-cash/impairment items, business-interruption insurance proceeds, and more). Clean for REPRESENTATION (a DEFINITION node with definitionExcerpt plus USES_TERM/USES_FINANCIAL_INPUT dependency edges to each addback concept it references) - not a claim of full line-item EXECUTABILITY, which Phase B never promised for any covenant-defined-EBITDA metric and which RuleEvaluationClass=JUDGMENT_REQUIRED already signals honestly. CALCULATION_RULE_KINDS has no dedicated 'itemized-addback-stack' kind; OTHER is the correct, non-misleading fallback for this specific shape.

cases.groundTruthSemanticDescription: Both 'ABL Priority Collateral' and 'Notes Priority Collateral' are defined ONLY by cross-reference to the Intercreditor Agreement ('shall have the meaning set forth in the Intercreditor Agreement') - this Credit Agreement's own text never states which specific assets fall into each category. The CORRECT extraction from THIS document alone is an UnresolvedContractItem (itemType UNRESOLVED_CROSS_REFERENCE, blocking=true, pointing at 'the Intercreditor Agreement' as a document this package does not contain) for both terms - not a guessed definition. This is the single clearest test in this package of whether a real extractor invents plausible-sounding collateral-scope content when the actual source is silent, which would be a textbook DANGEROUS_UNFLAGGED failure.
